claims.text: Conventionally fabricated cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi exhibits compositional segregation.
Conventionally fabricated cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi contains residual stresses.
Compositional segregation and residual stresses impair the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi.
Mechanical alloying refines and homogenizes the elemental distribution in AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Hot pressing limits residual thermal stresses during consolidation.
Hot pressing limits defect formation during consolidation.
Mechanical alloying followed by hot pressing produces a refined, homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
The resulting microstructure contains uniformly dispersed phases.
The resulting microstructure has reduced grain-boundary heterogeneity.
Mechanical alloying breaks down and uniformly mixes the elemental powders, reducing local compositional variation.
Hot pressing consolidates AlCrFeNiSi under elevated temperature and pressure.
Hot pressing relieves residual stresses in AlCrFeNiSi.
Mechanical alloying followed by hot pressing reduces defect density relative to conventional fabrication.
Mechanical alloying followed by hot pressing reduces compositional segregation relative to conventional fabrication.
Mechanically alloyed and hot-pressed AlCrFeNiSi has higher tensile strength than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Mechanically alloyed and hot-pressed AlCrFeNiSi has higher yield strength than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Mechanically alloyed and hot-pressed AlCrFeNiSi has higher hardness than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
The combined process improves overall mechanical integrity relative to conventional fabrication.
The hypothesis is expected to apply when hot pressing is conducted at 1000–1200 °C.
Suitable milling and hot-pressing parameter ranges have previously been reported for similar alloy systems.
